hold: Stand your marks where the last one has stopped being useful, and not before.
Raise nothing. Not a house, not a claim, not on any shore.
You cannot name what you mark. A standing wants somebody else to come back to it.

beats.title: You did not land
body: Seafarer and Cairnwright and Riskweaver did not come ashore from anything. They are aground on the near shore, with what the wreck spilled on the beach and no boat coming.
There is no company to vote with and nothing here that wants building. What there is, is a hull on its side that somebody could put back together.

beats.title: A stone on the cairn
body: Riskweaver carried a stone up and put it on the heap. Nobody asked them to and nothing in the near shore works better for it.

A cairn is not built by anybody. It is what is left when everybody who was here has put one on, and the only thing it counts is how many of them there were — which is why it is the one thing in this valley that is not raised by a vote, a trade, or a day’s work.

beats.title: She will float
body: Seafarer has brought the hull up to 1.00, past the mark this valley calls sound at 0.85.

Seaworthy here means the settlement has stopped offering to mend her. It is the same number the repair list has always used, asked the other way round — and she can fall back under it, because wear does not care what she was this morning.

beats.title: Nothing keeps in a sack
body: Riskweaver was carrying food and it went soft before they ate it. Until now a pack was the one place in this valley where nothing ever spoiled — better than the open store, better than a shed, better than anywhere a settlement could build.
It is the store’s job to keep things and the granary’s job to keep them longer. What is in your arms is only ever on its way somewhere.

beats.title: A trade
body: Riskweaver and Cairnwright have swapped 2 food for 5 wood. Nobody minted anything, nobody agreed a price, and both of them are better off than they were.
This is what an economy is before there is any money in it. Everything else — coin, a rate, a market — is a convenience laid on top of two people seeing the sense in it.

beats.title: Stacked outside
body: Riskweaver carried a load to the boat, found no room in it, and put 2 of it on the ground beside the door. It is still there. It is just not under anything.

Nothing here holds anything by default — a boat holds twenty and a corner of somebody’s house holds twelve. Anybody hauling past will get that stack in on the day there is room for it, and the weather is working on it until somebody does.

beats.title: Somebody who is good at something
body: Riskweaver has made 13 things now and there is nobody on this coast better at farming. It is not a title anybody gave them. It is the count.
A settlement where everybody is equally mediocre at everything has no reason to ask anybody in particular for anything. This one now has somebody to ask.

beats.title: Somebody changed trade
body: Riskweaver came ashore a scout and has spent long enough at something else that it is what they are: a farmer, by the count of what they have actually done.
Nothing in this valley assigned them that and nothing can take it away. It is the same for every trade that has not been invented here yet — whoever ends up doing it will be the one who did it.

beats.title: It does not keep
body: 7 food gathered in the near shore has gone soft in the sack before anybody got to it. Nobody did anything wrong: berries in a bag on the ground are berries in a bag on the ground.
Somewhere dry to keep it is a building, and a building past a house is something this settlement has to vote for. Until then every hour spent gathering is an hour with a hole in it.

beats.title: The stack outside
body: the near shore has been putting what will not fit on the ground beside the store, and the ground has started taking it. It is not gone the moment it is set down — anybody hauling past will get it back in the day there is room for it — but a heap on a wet coast is on a clock.
Somewhere to put things is a building, and a building past a house is something this settlement has to vote for.

beats.title: It takes things
body: Cairnwright was out past the settlement with a full pack when it turned, and came back with less than they set out to carry. Until now the weather here could make a day long and could make a roof rot, and it could not take anything out of anybody’s hands.

There are two answers to it and the settlement has to vote for either. Somewhere to put a load down out at the workings is one. Knowing at first light that it was going to turn is the other, and it is the one that gets the load home.

beats.title: The first winter
body: The berries have stopped coming back and the wood is slow. What is in the stores is what there is until the thaw.
This is what the granary was for, and the shelter out at the workings, and every argument anybody had about laying something by. A settlement that voted those down finds out now.

beats.title: Somebody who is good at something
body: Seafarer has made 13 things now and there is nobody on this coast better at forestry. It is not a title anybody gave them. It is the count.
A settlement where everybody is equally mediocre at everything has no reason to ask anybody in particular for anything. This one now has somebody to ask.

beats.title: Somebody who is good at something
body: Riskweaver has made 13 things now and there is nobody on this coast better at hauling. It is not a title anybody gave them. It is the count.
A settlement where everybody is equally mediocre at everything has no reason to ask anybody in particular for anything. This one now has somebody to ask.

chronicle.title: You did not land
body: Seafarer and Cairnwright and Riskweaver did not come ashore from anything. They are aground on the near shore, with what the wreck spilled on the beach and no boat coming.
There is no company to vote with and nothing here that wants building. What there is, is a hull on its side that somebody could put back together.

chronicle.title: A stone on the cairn
body: Riskweaver carried a stone up and put it on the heap. Nobody asked them to and nothing in the near shore works better for it.

A cairn is not built by anybody. It is what is left when everybody who was here has put one on, and the only thing it counts is how many of them there were — which is why it is the one thing in this valley that is not raised by a vote, a trade, or a day’s work.

chronicle.title: She will float
body: Seafarer has brought the hull up to 1.00, past the mark this valley calls sound at 0.85.

Seaworthy here means the settlement has stopped offering to mend her. It is the same number the repair list has always used, asked the other way round — and she can fall back under it, because wear does not care what she was this morning.

chronicle.title: Nothing keeps in a sack
body: Riskweaver was carrying food and it went soft before they ate it. Until now a pack was the one place in this valley where nothing ever spoiled — better than the open store, better than a shed, better than anywhere a settlement could build.
It is the store’s job to keep things and the granary’s job to keep them longer. What is in your arms is only ever on its way somewhere.

chronicle.title: A trade
body: Riskweaver and Cairnwright have swapped 2 food for 5 wood. Nobody minted anything, nobody agreed a price, and both of them are better off than they were.
This is what an economy is before there is any money in it. Everything else — coin, a rate, a market — is a convenience laid on top of two people seeing the sense in it.

chronicle.title: Stacked outside
body: Riskweaver carried a load to the boat, found no room in it, and put 2 of it on the ground beside the door. It is still there. It is just not under anything.

Nothing here holds anything by default — a boat holds twenty and a corner of somebody’s house holds twelve. Anybody hauling past will get that stack in on the day there is room for it, and the weather is working on it until somebody does.

chronicle.title: Somebody who is good at something
body: Riskweaver has made 13 things now and there is nobody on this coast better at farming. It is not a title anybody gave them. It is the count.
A settlement where everybody is equally mediocre at everything has no reason to ask anybody in particular for anything. This one now has somebody to ask.

chronicle.title: Somebody changed trade
body: Riskweaver came ashore a scout and has spent long enough at something else that it is what they are: a farmer, by the count of what they have actually done.
Nothing in this valley assigned them that and nothing can take it away. It is the same for every trade that has not been invented here yet — whoever ends up doing it will be the one who did it.

chronicle.title: It does not keep
body: 7 food gathered in the near shore has gone soft in the sack before anybody got to it. Nobody did anything wrong: berries in a bag on the ground are berries in a bag on the ground.
Somewhere dry to keep it is a building, and a building past a house is something this settlement has to vote for. Until then every hour spent gathering is an hour with a hole in it.

chronicle.title: The stack outside
body: the near shore has been putting what will not fit on the ground beside the store, and the ground has started taking it. It is not gone the moment it is set down — anybody hauling past will get it back in the day there is room for it — but a heap on a wet coast is on a clock.
Somewhere to put things is a building, and a building past a house is something this settlement has to vote for.

chronicle.title: It takes things
body: Cairnwright was out past the settlement with a full pack when it turned, and came back with less than they set out to carry. Until now the weather here could make a day long and could make a roof rot, and it could not take anything out of anybody’s hands.

There are two answers to it and the settlement has to vote for either. Somewhere to put a load down out at the workings is one. Knowing at first light that it was going to turn is the other, and it is the one that gets the load home.
